compliance_human_subjects_research: Morgan State University requires all research involving human subjects to be reviewed and approved by the Institutional Review Board (IRB) in compliance with federal regulations at 45 CFR 46. The Office of Research Compliance (ORC) oversees this process. Submissions must include the research protocol and consent forms. Researchers should allow at least 30 days for review, after which the IRB notifies them in writing of approval, disapproval, or conditional approval. No human subjects research may begin without IRB approval. The IRB Administrator can be reached at irb.research@morgan.edu. Five required forms govern the lifecycle of human-subjects studies at Morgan: (1) Human Subjects Research Approval Request Form (new protocol); (2) Human Subjects Research Approval Renewal Form (annual continuing review); (3) Human Subjects Research Protocol Amendment/Modification Form (changes to approved protocols); (4) Human Subjects Research Reportable Events Form (adverse events, unanticipated problems); (5) Human Research Protection Program Closure Form (study close-out, submitted via a Google Form at forms.gle/DgqtsWKViCeodgLx6). Supporting guidance documents include the IRB Process Synopsis (PDF dated 2023-03-21), the IRB Exempt Research Categories memo (dated 2022-12-12), the BOR-approved Protection of Human Subjects in Research Policy (2020), the Protection of Human Subjects in Research Procedures (2021), and the CITI Training Program instructions (2023-01-06). CITI Training: All personnel engaged in human-subjects research — Principal Investigators, Co-PIs, research staff, individuals obtaining informed consent, contact persons in recruitment materials, and faculty advisors — must complete the CITI Human Subjects Research (HSR) course before submitting an IRB application or accessing private identifiable data. Researchers select the learner group matching their discipline (Biomedical, Social Behavioral Education, etc.). PIs, Co-PIs, and Faculty Advisors are always considered engaged in research due to their oversight responsibilities. PIs are responsible for confirming that all research personnel complete required training at citiprogram.org. RCR and COI CITI courses are strongly encouraged. IRB Committee composition under 45 CFR 46 requires at least five members including scientific and nonscientific representatives, multiple professions, and at least one unaffiliated member. The current Chair is Benjamin Welsh, Ph.D. (Associate Professor, Education). The IRB has 14 voting members spanning Community Health and Policy, Sociology, Psychology, Biology, Architecture, Nursing, Social Work, Education, and CMNS, plus a non-affiliated community member. Quorum is greater than 50% of voting members. The IRB meets monthly per a published calendar (e.g., 2025-2026 meeting dates run from August 27, 2025 through June 17, 2026 with application deadlines roughly two to three weeks prior). External (non-Morgan) investigators seeking to recruit MSU students, faculty, or staff must contact irb.research@morgan.edu before beginning recruitment and provide a recruitment-strategy memorandum, home-IRB approval letter and protocol number, IRB application, consent forms, recruitment materials, instruments, and other supporting documents. Recruitment may not begin until written site authorization is granted by the University's Authorized Institutional Official. Key staff: Institutional Official is Willie May, Ph.D. (Vice President for Research and Economic Development). The Acting Director for Research Compliance is Keyshawn Moncrieffe, Ph.D., MBA, CCEP, CRA, who assumed the role after Dr. Edet Isuk's retirement on 2026-01-01. The Research Compliance Assistant is Olatunde Aladesote.

ora_history:
The Office of Sponsored Programs and Research (OSPR) was established in 1988 under Dr. Edet Isuk as Founding Director, with one secretarial assistant. Prior to this, no dedicated office at Morgan State managed research proposals for external funding. Annual extramural funding averaged $7 million at inception.

From 1988 to 1997, OSPR reported to the Dean of Graduate Studies and handled proposal development, budget preparation, and post-award management.

In 1997, Dr. Henry Williams joined as Assistant Vice President for Sponsored Programs, elevating the office's status to report directly to the Vice President for Academic Affairs. Staff expanded to 11 members and annual funding grew to $24 million. Responsibilities broadened to include research compliance, contracts management, and business development.

From 2002 to 2020, Dr. Mildred Ofosu served as AVP for Research, maintaining consistent growth and reaching approximately $30 million in annual extramural funding. Title III programs were reassigned to Academic Affairs early in her tenure.

In 2012, President Wilson created the Division of Research and Economic Development (D-RED), with Dr. Victor McCrary as inaugural Vice President from 2012 to 2018.

In 2018, Dr. Willie May, former NIST Director, became Vice President for Research. Under his leadership, the office was renamed from OSPR to the Office of Research Administration (ORA) in 2020, with Dr. Farin Kamangar appointed Assistant Vice President.

Major recent funding acquisitions include GESTAR II ($28M), ASCEND expansion ($17M), RCMI ($15M), and ONR AI/ML research ($9M), reaching $72 million in new commitments by 2022.

post_award_notification_and_setup:
Notification of Award: Award notifications may take the form of an award letter, a purchase order, a detailed contract, or an agreement spelling out the terms and conditions. The notification is directed to the Assistant VP for Research Administration, who distributes copies to the PI/PD and the VP for Finance and Management. The Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) is also notified.

Important: Awards for proposals that did not undergo the normal internal processing, review, and approval through the Office of Research Administration (ORA) may be refused by the University.

Set-Up of Award: Once the award is formally accepted, documents are forwarded to RFA, which assigns an Index or Budget code number and establishes the account in Banner (the University's financial system). The Comptroller's Office is notified. Account setup typically takes up to three (3) business days. A Post-Award Briefing meeting is then scheduled with the PI and supporting units.

Post-Award Briefing: The Post-Award Briefing provides a roadmap in administering and managing key grant/contract post-award activities, spanning from account setup through final reporting. Primary offices involved in the briefing are:
- Office of Research Administration (ORA)
- Office of Human Resources
- Office of Procurement
- Office of the Comptroller
- Purchasing Card Office

Contacts: ORA — Tyler Hall, Student Service Bldg, Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251. Phone 443-885-4044. Fax 443-885-8280. Email ask.ora@morgan.edu. Research Compliance Director: Dr. Edet Isuk — edet.isuk@morgan.edu.
post_award_reporting:
Reporting Overview. After an award is issued, funding agencies monitor both programmatic and financial aspects of a project. PIs/PDs prepare technical (programmatic) reports submitted to funding agencies at intervals specified in the Notice of Award (NoA) — monthly, quarterly, annually, or at grant closeout. The Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) handles fiscal reports; PIs are responsible for verifying the accuracy of expenses.

Common report types:
- Programmatic: annual progress reports, final technical reports, invention reports, property/equipment reports.
- Financial: annual financial reports, final financial reports, invoicing.

Programmatic Reporting Requirements: Final reports are normally due within 90 days after the end of the project period, and usually include the technical, property (major equipment), and invention reports. Report categories include Interim/Progress reports, Final Technical Reporting, Invention Reporting, and Final Reports / Closeout.

Effort Reporting and Certification:
- Schedule: Effort certifications are generated three times per year — February (Fall semester), July (Spring semester), and October (Summer effort).
- Deadline: Once released to campus, certifications must be completed within 14 calendar days.
- Platform: Searchlight.
- Who must certify: All PIs/PDs, faculty, professional staff, and students paid directly from federal grants and contracts.
- Definition: Effort is the amount of time spent on a particular activity. It includes time working on a sponsored project where salary is directly charged or cost-shared effort (also known as match).

Cost Sharing: Cost sharing represents that portion of the total project costs of a sponsored agreement that are not charged to the sponsor. These costs are absorbed by the University rather than by the sponsor.

Compliance framework: All reporting is governed by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidelines, including 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance).

References: PI Handbook 5: Policies & Guidelines (PDF) — Effort Reporting on page 96, Cost Sharing on page 36. URL: https://www.morgan.edu/Documents/ADMINISTRATION/OFFICES/ora/PI/2024-07-01_PIHandbook5.pdf. PI Handbook 3: Grant-Related Processes (2025-02-24) covers post-award report mechanics.

Additional details (Programmatic Reporting accordion): Property and Invention reports must be completed even when the project acquired no equipment and produced no invention. PIs should treat the requirement seriously — failure to submit reports on time may adversely affect future prospects for funding from the agency. The schedule for required technical reports is typically incorporated in the award document from the sponsor.

Additional details (Effort Reporting accordion): Effort certifications cover employees paid from federal AND state contracts or grants, including any mandatory cost sharing accounts. PIs/PDs (or their approved designee, called an 'alternate certifier') must verify and certify the reports, attesting that employees actually performed the work on the indicated accounts in the same percentage of time. Any corrections to effort should be reported immediately to the ORA Director (Gillian.Silver@morgan.edu) and to the Grant Accountant assigned to the grant in Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA). PIs/PDs and alternate certifiers are notified via email from the Searchlight platform when reports are available. The electronic effort report may be certified by the employee, supervisor, or PI/PD who has personal familiarity with the employee's compensated effort. The report is after-the-fact and is generated from historical payroll data.

Additional details (Cost Sharing): Cost sharing can be required by the sponsor or volunteered by a PI/PD; regardless, any commitment of effort referenced in the project proposal or award document must be honored, reported, and captured in the effort reporting system. Because faculty, administrative, and clerical salaries at MSU are paid by the employee's department, cost-shared effort represents a redirection of departmental resources from teaching or other departmental activities to support sponsored agreements.

pre_award_budget_development:
Comprehensive guidance for preparing the budget (also called the cost proposal) for a Morgan State University sponsored project. ORA emphasizes that the budget is equally as important as the technical proposal. For questions contact ask.ora@morgan.edu or 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280).

Budget overview: Budgets are comprehensive planning documents integrating details for achieving proposal objectives, accounting for both long-range goals and short-term targets. A budget typically includes direct costs, other direct costs, indirect costs, and other budget elements.

Expense categories:

Personnel salaries and wages: senior personnel, post-doctoral researchers, lab technicians, graduate/undergraduate students, teaching assistants, and clerical staff.

Fringe benefits (current rates): Regular full-time/non-contractual employees (year round) = 42% of gross salary; Faculty during academic year = 42%; Faculty during summer = 9%; Contractual employees (year round) = 9%. See the Fringe Benefit Rate page for the official rate letter.

Equipment: defined as property with acquisition cost of $5,000 or more and an expected service life exceeding one year. Brief descriptions and justifications are required.

Travel: includes domestic and international travel for fieldwork and conferences. Current 2025 reimbursable rates under the State of Maryland include personal automobile mileage at $0.70 per mile, and meal per diems of $15 (breakfast), $18 (lunch), and $30 (dinner) for a total of $63 daily. GSA Per Diem Rates and the MSU University Travel page are also referenced.

Participant support: costs that defray expenses for students in training activities, conferences, or symposiums. Participants must be non-MSU employees receiving services (not providing them). Morgan employees do not qualify as participants, and indirect costs are not allowed on participant support.

Materials and supplies: supplies, printing, instructional materials, and audiovisual/computer supplies.

Consultant services: require descriptions of proposed services, time estimates, and payment rates. MSU faculty may not be listed as consultants.

Subawards (also called subgrants, subagreements, or subcontracts): require clear budget provisions, separate identification, and a service explanation. See the Pre-Award Subawards page.

Facilities and Administrative (F&A) / Indirect Cost: Morgan State's currently negotiated rate for Organized Research (On-Campus) is 53%-54% of modified total direct cost (see the F&A Cost Rates page for the full rate schedule by fiscal year and activity type).

Linked templates and resources from this page: PI Handbook 2 (Grant Budgets) PDF, NSF Budget Template (protected Excel), Budget Justification Template (Word), and Budget Preparation PowerPoint Slides PDF.
pre_award_internal_routing_form:
The Internal Routing Form (IRF) is a required document that must be submitted before applying for any external funding, preferably two weeks prior to the sponsor's submission deadline. The IRF gives the Office of Research Administration basic information about the Principal Investigator and the funding opportunity, captures certifications regarding Responsible Conduct of Research standards, and confirms supervisory approval to proceed with the project. The IRF is completed via DocuSign; questions can be directed to Ms. Deshun Li (deshun.li@morgan.edu) or ask.ora@morgan.edu, 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280).

The IRF includes the following sections:
- MSU Principal Investigator details: name, school, department, contact information.
- Funding Opportunity information: FOA URL, program name, CFDA/ALN number, sponsor type, and due date.
- Application details: project title, MSU role, work location, submission type, activity type, funding amounts, and proposed start date.
- Partner PI & Institution information: required only for subawards.
- Restrictions: six surety questions covering federal/state bar status, criminal convictions, indictments, foreign nationals, and conflicts of interest.
- Requirements: cost share, resource needs, equipment purchases, utilities, personnel, human subjects research, animal research, radioactive materials, and faculty release time.
- Certification statements: affirm project discussion with department leadership, accuracy of information, and acceptance of scientific responsibility.

After the IRF is submitted, the PI must send a Budget (Excel) and Budget Justification (Word) to the ORA Budget Specialist (see the Budget Development page). The IRF must collect signatures from the PI/PD, Department Chair, Dean or Center Director, ORA Research Budget Specialist, Grants Manager, and Director of Research Administration.

pre_award_overview:
Morgan State University requires all sponsored project proposals to undergo review and approval through the Office of Research Administration (ORA). The Pre-Award section provides information and resources for complete proposal development, including preparation tools, institutional data, sponsor information, and necessary forms. Faculty, PIs, and research staff can reach ORA at ask.ora@morgan.edu or by phone at 443-885-4044.

Proposal development process: Resources include PI Handbooks, trainings, and access to the Pivot-RP Funding Opportunities Database (https://pivot.proquest.com/dashboard). Researchers should review proposal components and the submission checklist, then develop budgets according to university guidelines. ORA offers tips for timely proposal submission presented by staff specialists.

Intention to submit: An Internal Routing Form (IRF) initiates the proposal review process and should be submitted at least two weeks before the agency deadline. Concurrent submission of the budget (Excel format) and the budget justification (Word format) to designated ORA staff is required.

Application information available on this site: University application information (UEI, EIN, NAICS, SAM expiration, etc.), the current fringe benefit rate schedule, and the Facilities & Administrative (F&A) cost rates are all documented resources for proposal budgeting. Ms. Deshun Li and Ailing Zhang, MS are referenced as ORA pre-award contacts. Pre-award spending information and advance account creation are addressed in a dedicated section, and pre-award subaward procedures are covered separately. A Limited Submission policy applies when sponsors cap how many proposals MSU may submit.

Subpages: University Application Information, Role of Principal Investigator, Proposal Components, Proposal Submission Checklist, Internal Routing Form, Budget Development, Fringe Benefit Rate, F&A Cost Rates, Proposal and Budget Examples, Pre-Award Spending, Pre-Award Subawards, and Limited Submission.
pre_award_proposal_components:
Technical components typically required for a research proposal at Morgan State University. ORA emphasizes that each Funding Opportunity Announcement (FoA) has specific requirements, so applicants must thoroughly review the relevant FoA before drafting. Contact ORA at ask.ora@morgan.edu or 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280) for assistance.

Standard proposal components:

Abstract / Executive Summary: A concise summary written within sponsor-specified space limits, covering the problem, objectives, approach, and project cost. The abstract should be clear and should accurately reflect and parallel the content of the proposal.

Introduction / Background: Demonstrates knowledge of the field, identifies research gaps, and establishes project importance while relating specific aims to broader long-term goals.

Goals & Objectives: Specifies broad long-term goals and expected outcomes, followed by clear, brief, realistic, and measurable specific objectives.

Methodology: Explains how objectives will be achieved, relating the proposed approach to specific objectives and justifying the selection of methods.

Key Personnel: Describes qualifications, relevant experience, and specific roles of all key personnel. List the Principal Investigator first. Include any personnel critical to project success even if their salary is not being requested from the sponsor.

Evaluation: For training or demonstration projects, the evaluation section relates evaluation methods to stated objectives and describes data collection, timelines, resources, and intended use of results.

Office: Tyler Hall, Suite 304. Phone: 443-885-1313. Email: keyshawn.moncrieffe@morgan.edu.

Dr. Keyshawn Moncrieffe serves as Acting Director for Research Compliance at Morgan State University. She provides oversight of programs that promote ethical and compliant research — including human research protections (IRB), responsible conduct of research (RCR), financial conflict of interest, export controls, and research security.

Dr. Moncrieffe brings extensive experience in research administration, compliance program operations, and project management, advancing Morgan State's mission to foster a culture of research integrity and excellence.

Education: PhD in Higher Education (Advanced Studies Leadership & Policy), Morgan State University; MBA, Morgan State University; MHS, University of Maryland, Baltimore (pending).

Certifications: Certified Research Administrator (CRA) (Research Administrators Certification Council; Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP) (Society of Corporate Compliance & Ethics.

trainings_overview:
The Morgan State University Office of Research Administration (ORA) offers a comprehensive trainings program covering all aspects of administrative functions related to research at the university. The trainings page describes offerings as covering 'All Aspects of Administrative Functions at Morgan State University' and includes faculty/staff development videos, presentations, and workshops on research administration subjects.

The ORA training catalog is organized into the following eight sections:

1) SPARK — Sponsored Projects Administration Readiness and Knowledge: the training program for Morgan State University research staff and administrators.

2) e-Training (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/e-training) — A gamut of self-paced eTraining modules touching on all aspects of administrative functions: Post Award Quick Guide; Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration; Building the Project Team (contractual hiring, summer contracts, honoraria); Travel on Sponsored Projects; Purchasing with Purpose (procurement, Banner Pool Level 08, subawards); Supporting Participants (stipends, tuition, MTDC); Show Your Work (time and effort reporting); It Takes a Village (cost share).

3) Research Compliance and Security Training (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/research-compliance/research-security/research-compliance-and-security-training) — REQUIRED for all MSU personnel engaged in federally funded research. Options include CITI Program (https://citiprogram.org/), NSF SECURE Center (https://www.secure-center.org/ctm), and NSF Modules (https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training). Personnel must complete one approved option and retain the certificate.

4) New Faculty Development Seminars (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/new-faculty-development-seminars) — Seminar series for new faculty covering the grant lifecycle, funding sources, proposal components, research/fiscal compliance, pedagogy, AI in research, the history of Morgan, and professional societies/fellowships. Presenters include Dr. Farin Kamangar, Gillian Silver, Laura Dorsey-Elson, Dr. Edet Isuk, and Dr. Edwin Johnson.

5) Monthly D-RED Seminars (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/monthly-d-red-seminars) — Recurring monthly seminars on research administration topics. The pattern is typically the second Wednesday of each month (recent dates include Sep 10, Oct 9, Nov 12, Dec 11). Topics range from NSF funding strategy and CAREER awards, to research security, cost sharing, audits, intellectual property, export controls, conflict of interest, and time and effort reporting. Past PDFs and Zoom recordings are archived going back to 2019.

6) Special Workshops (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/special-workshops) — One-off topical workshops. An example documented workshop is the Cost Allowability workshop held December 9, 2022, with presentations from Farin Kamangar, Gillian Silver, Becca Steiner, Lucy Manyara, and Shamon Shine-Lee.

7) Test Prep (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/test-prep) — Study materials to prepare ORA staff for the Research Administrators Certification Council (RACC) credentials: CRA® (Certified Research Administrator), CPRA® (Certified Pre-Award Research Administrator), and CFRA® (Certified Financial Research Administrator). RACC website: https://www.cra-cert.org/. Fifteen chapter-based PDF study guides are provided.

8) Trainings Outside ORA (https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/msu-trainings-outside-ora) — Pointers to research-relevant trainings offered by other MSU units, including the ASCEND and RCMI Fall 2023 Faculty Development Opportunities newsletter.

ORA training coordinators and frequent presenters include Dr. Farin Kamangar (MD, PhD, CRA, CPRA, CFRA — Associate Vice President for Research), Gillian Silver (MPH, CPH, CRA, CPRA, CFRA), Ryan Mobley (CRA, CFRA, CPRA), and Rebecca (Becca) Steiner. General contact for trainings: Office of Research Administration, Tyler Hall, Student Service Bldg, Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251. Phone 443-885-4044. Fax 443-885-8280. Email ask.ora@morgan.edu.
trainings_test_prep:
At Morgan State University, many faculty and staff play vital roles in coordinating, managing, and administering sponsored awards, including grants, cooperative agreements, and contracts. ORA's Test Prep program supports those staff in pursuing professional certification through the Research Administrators Certification Council (RACC). RACC website: https://www.cra-cert.org/.

RACC offers three credentials, each with its own exam:
- CRA® — Certified Research Administrator: https://www.cra-cert.org/cra-
- CPRA® — Certified Pre-Award Research Administrator: https://www.cra-cert.org/cpra-
- CFRA® — Certified Financial Research Administrator: https://www.cra-cert.org/cfra

ORA provides 15 chapter-based PDF study guides covering the topics required across the RACC exam blueprints. Each chapter includes background information, test questions, and answers. The study chapters cover:

1) F&A Costs (Facilities and Administrative costs / indirect costs)
2) Prior Approval
3) Cost Share
4) SBIR/STTR (Small Business Innovation Research / Technology Transfer)
5) NIH (National Institutes of Health)
6) NSF (National Science Foundation)
7) Award Instruments
8) Cost Allowability
9) Intellectual Property
10) Single Audit
11) Notices of Award
12) Research Misconduct
13) Human Research Ethics
14) Animal Research Ethics
15) Export Controls
